# Architecture Review

The architecture review validates that the complete body of architectural decisions
covers all game design requirements, is internally consistent, and correctly targets
the project's pinned engine version. It is the quality gate between Technical Setup
and Pre-Production.

**Argument modes:**
- **No argument / `full`**: Full review — all phases
- **`coverage`**: Traceability only — which GDD requirements have no ADR
- **`consistency`**: Cross-ADR conflict detection only
- **`engine`**: Engine compatibility audit only
- **`single-gdd [path]`**: Review architecture coverage for one specific GDD
- **`rtm`**: Requirements Traceability Matrix — extends the standard matrix
  to include story file paths and test file paths; outputs
  `docs/architecture/requirements-traceability.md` with the full
  GDD requirement → ADR → Story → Test chain. Use in Production phase when
  stories and tests exist.

---

Every `AskUserQuestion` call follows `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md`
(collaborative asks always · guided major-only · autonomous logs and proceeds;
`automation_always_ask` categories always prompt).

**`workflow`** (see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`):
- `full` — full traceability matrix across all GDDs and all ADRs.
- `standard` — reduced scope: architecture doc + critical ADRs only.
- `minimal` — not applicable (no architecture doc required).

## Phase 1: Load Everything

## Phase 5: Engine Compatibility Cross-Check

## Phase 6: Architecture Document Coverage

## Phase 7: Output the Review Report

## Phase 8: Write and Update Traceability Index

## Phase 9: Handoff

**Read `references/9-handoff.md` now and follow it** — this phase's steps are in that file, not here. Read it again if the conversation was compacted or resumed during this phase.

## Error Recovery Protocol

**First, verify the artifact.** If the return contract named a path, check the
path exists before treating the phase as done — **a named artifact that is not
on disk is a failed phase, however fluent the response reads.** An agent can
burn a full phase and return a plausible preamble having written nothing, which
is neither BLOCKED nor an error nor "fails to complete", so the trigger below
never fires. Resume it naming the unmet contract; the context is
usually still there.

If any spawned agent returns BLOCKED, errors, or fails to complete: **surface it
immediately, don't proceed past a dependency it blocks, and always produce a
partial report** (retry scope here = fewer GDDs / single-system). Full procedure:
`.claude/docs/error-recovery-protocol.md`.

---

## Collaborative Protocol

**Applies in `collaborative` mode (the default).** For `guided` and
`autonomous` modes, see `.claude/docs/automation-modes.md` — the rules below
describe what collaborative mode requires, not universal behavior.

1. **Read silently** — do not narrate every file read
2. **Show the matrix** — present the full traceability matrix before any write
   approval; let the user see the state
3. **Don't guess** — if a requirement is ambiguous, ask: "Is [X] a technical
   requirement or a design preference?"
4. **Draft before approval** — always show the content that will be written (the
   report, the updated ADR section, the systems-index row) inline in the conversation
   before requesting approval. Never ask to write something the user has not yet seen.
5. **Use `AskUserQuestion` for write approvals** — plain text "May I?" is not
   sufficient. Use the structured tool with labeled options [A]/[B]/[C] so the
   user can choose between "write now", "show full draft first", and "not yet".
   Multi-file changesets must list every file and what changes, then ask once
   with grouped options — not a separate plain-text question per file.
6. **Non-blocking** — the verdict is advisory; the user decides whether to continue
   despite CONCERNS or even FAIL findings

# /architecture-review — Phase 1: Load Everything

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 1: Load Everything

**In this file:**

- Phase 1a — L0: Summary Scan (fast, low tokens)
- Phase 1b — L1/L2: Targeted Section Load
- Design Documents
- Architecture Documents
- Engine Reference
- Project Standards

### Phase 1a — L0: Summary Scan (fast, low tokens)

**Freshness check before any scan.** Locate the latest prior report — Glob
`docs/architecture/architecture-review-*.md` and take the newest — then:

```
Bash: bash .claude/scripts/review-receipts.sh check "[latest-report]" docs/architecture/adr-*.md design/gdd/*.md
```

- **Any `UNRESOLVED`** — check this FIRST; it disqualifies every option
  below. One of the two globs matched no file, so that whole document class
  was never examined and the comparison covered less than it appears to.
  Say which pattern came back unresolved and stop: an ADR or GDD directory
  that is empty, renamed or misspelled is a finding about the project, not a
  reason to stand on a prior report. Never read a set of `UNCHANGED` lines as
  "everything is current" while an `UNRESOLVED` line is present — the set
  compared was not the set requested.
- **Everything `UNCHANGED`** (and no `UNRESOLVED`) — nothing this review
  reads has changed since that report; re-running reproduces it. Surface the
  prior report's date and verdict and offer via `AskUserQuestion`: `[A] Stand
  on the prior report (Recommended)` / `[B] Re-run the full review anyway` —
  `guided` proceeds with [A] and notes it; `autonomous` logs via
  `log_decision` and stands on the prior report.
- **Some `CHANGED`/`NEW`** — name them, then scope instead of re-running
  everything: recommend `/architecture-review [system]` (single-system mode)
  for just the changed systems. A full re-run stays available on request,
  and structural changes (a `NEW` ADR, a deleted file) warrant one.
- **`RECEIPT: NONE`** — no prior report, or one written before receipts
  existed. Proceed with the full review; this run's report will carry the
  first stamps.

Before reading any full document, use Grep to extract `## Summary` sections
from all GDDs and ADRs:

```
Grep pattern="## Summary" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -A 4
Grep pattern="## Summary" glob="docs/architecture/adr-*.md" output_mode="content" -A 3
```

**Fail open on a missing Summary.** Establish the denominator: glob
`design/gdd/*.md` and count **N**. A scan matching fewer than N means those GDDs
predate `## Summary` (`/design-system` emits it, but older GDDs lack it) — never
treat an absent Summary as a system out of scope. A zero-match scan means "no GDD
carries a Summary yet", not "nothing to review": full-read the unmatched set.

For `single-gdd [path]` mode: use the target GDD's summary to identify which
ADRs reference the same system (Grep ADRs for the system name), then load only
those ADRs' sections per Phase 1b. Skip unrelated GDDs entirely.

For `engine` mode: load ADR sections only — GDDs are not needed for engine checks.
In practice this is the `## Engine Compatibility` scan alone.

For `coverage` or `full` mode: proceed to Phase 1b for the full in-scope set.
**This is a section load, not a full-file load** — see below for why, and for the
narrow cases that still justify escalating to a whole document.

### Phase 1b — L1/L2: Targeted Section Load

Load the sections the later phases actually consume — **not whole files**. This
skill reads the two largest document sets in the project (every GDD *and* every
ADR); at realistic sizes a full load of both exhausts the context window before
Phase 2 starts, and most of what it loads is narrative this skill never uses.

**Establish the denominator first.** Glob `design/gdd/*.md` and count **N_gdd**;
glob `docs/architecture/adr-*.md` and count **N_adr**. Report both. A section
scan matching fewer than the denominator means those documents lack the section —
**never treat an absent section as an absent document.** The scan narrows the
*read* set; it never shrinks the *in-scope* set.

### Design Documents

Phase 2 extracts *technical requirements* — data structures, performance
constraints, engine capabilities, cross-system communication, persistence,
threading, platform needs. Those live in a known set of sections; Overview and
Player Fantasy are narrative and yield none.

```
Grep pattern="^## (Detailed Rules|Detailed Design|Formulas|Dependencies|Tuning Knobs|Acceptance Criteria)" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -A 40
```

Accept **either** `## Detailed Rules` or `## Detailed Design` — the design
standard and the GDD template disagree on the name and they denote the same
required section. Full-read a single GDD only when a scanned section
cross-references material outside itself, or when a GDD matched zero sections
(it predates the template — read it whole and say so).

- `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — the authoritative list of systems; read whole (small, and it is an index)

### Architecture Documents

Phases 3–5 need the traceability table, the decision itself, engine claims, and
the dependency edges — not Context, Consequences, Alternatives, Migration Plan or
Validation Criteria, which explain *why* a decision was made.

```
Grep pattern="^## (Status|Decision|GDD Requirements Addressed|Engine Compatibility|ADR Dependencies|Performance Implications)" glob="docs/architecture/adr-*.md" output_mode="content" -A 30
```

Interpret against **N_adr**, and distinguish the two zero-match cases — they are
not the same finding:

| Result | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| N_adr matches | Normal. | Proceed on the scanned sections. |
| Some ADRs match, some do not | Those ADRs are missing sections. | Record each as a **structural gap** in the Phase 7 report — a missing `## GDD Requirements Addressed` is itself a traceability finding. |
| **0 matches, N_adr > 0** | **Malformed ADRs**, not "no architecture". | "[N_adr] ADRs found, none carries a scannable section — run `/architecture-decision retrofit [file]` on each." Do **not** report zero coverage; that would read as a design failure when it is a format failure. |

Escalate to a full read of one ADR only when judging a conflict needs its
reasoning (Phase 4) — that is a per-ADR decision, not a blanket load.

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` if it exists

### Engine Reference
- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/VERSION.md`
- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/breaking-changes.md`
- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/deprecated-apis.md`
- **Only the module docs the in-scope ADRs actually name** — take the union of
  each ADR's `References Consulted` and `Post-Cutoff APIs Used` fields (already
  captured by the `## Engine Compatibility` scan above) and read those files.
  Reading the whole `modules/` directory loads engine subsystems the project may
  not use at all. If no ADR names any module, read none and note it: Phase 5
  cannot cross-check engine claims that were never made.

### Project Standards
- `project.yaml` — `naming.*` and `performance.*`; plus `.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` for those keys when absent and for forbidden patterns / allowed libraries

Report a count: "Loaded [N] GDDs, [M] ADRs, engine: [name + version]."

**Also read `docs/consistency-failures.md`** if it exists. Extract entries with
Domain matching the systems under review (Architecture, Engine, or any GDD domain
being covered). Surface recurring patterns as a "Known conflict-prone areas" note
at the top of the Phase 4 conflict detection output.

# /architecture-review — Phase 2: Extract Technical Requirements

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 2: Extract Technical Requirements from Every GDD

### Pre-load the TR Registry

Before extracting any requirements, read `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
if it exists. Index existing entries by `id` and by normalized `requirement`
text (lowercase, trimmed). This prevents ID renumbering across review runs.

For each requirement you extract, the matching rule is:
1. **Exact/near match** to an existing registry entry for the same system →
   reuse that entry's TR-ID unchanged. Update the `requirement` text in the
   registry only if the GDD wording changed (same intent, clearer phrasing) —
   add a `revised: [date]` field.
2. **No match** → assign a new ID: next available `TR-[system]-NNN` for that
   system, starting from the highest existing sequence + 1.
3. **Ambiguous** (partial match, intent unclear) → ask the user:
   > "Does '[new requirement text]' refer to the same requirement as
   > `TR-[system]-NNN: [existing text]'`, or is it a new requirement?"
   User answers: "Same requirement" (reuse ID) or "New requirement" (new ID).

For any requirement with `status: deprecated` in the registry — skip it.
It was removed from the GDD intentionally.

For each GDD, read it and extract all **technical requirements** — things the
architecture must provide for the system to work. A technical requirement is any
statement that implies a specific architectural decision.

Categories to extract:

| Category | Example |
|----------|---------|
| **Data structures** | "Each entity has health, max health, status effects" → needs a component/data schema |
| **Performance constraints** | "Collision detection must run at 60fps with 200 entities" → physics budget ADR |
| **Engine capability** | "Inverse kinematics for character animation" → IK system ADR |
| **Cross-system communication** | "Damage system notifies UI and audio simultaneously" → event/signal architecture ADR |
| **State persistence** | "Player progress persists between sessions" → save system ADR |
| **Threading/timing** | "AI decisions happen off the main thread" → concurrency ADR |
| **Platform requirements** | "Supports keyboard, gamepad, touch" → input system ADR |

For each GDD, produce a structured list:

```
GDD: [filename]
System: [system name]
Technical Requirements:
  TR-[GDD]-001: [requirement text] → Domain: [Physics/Rendering/etc]
  TR-[GDD]-002: [requirement text] → Domain: [...]
```

This becomes the **requirements baseline** — the complete set of what the
architecture must cover.

---
# /architecture-review — Phases 3 and 3b: Traceability Matrix and Story Linkage

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 3: Build the Traceability Matrix

**In this file:**

- Step 3b-1 — Load stories
- Step 3b-2 — Load test files
- Step 3b-3 — Build the extended RTM

For each technical requirement extracted in Phase 2, search the ADRs:

1. Use the ADRs **already loaded in Phase 1b** — do not re-read them. Extract each
   ADR's "GDD Requirements Addressed" section from what is already in context.
   (If Phase 1b ran in a mode that did not load every ADR, `Grep pattern="## GDD
   Requirements Addressed" glob="docs/architecture/adr-*.md" output_mode="content"
   -A 15` fills the gap without a full re-read.)
2. Check if it explicitly references the requirement or its GDD
3. Check if the ADR's decision text implicitly covers the requirement
4. Mark coverage status:

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| ✅ **Covered** | An **Accepted** ADR explicitly addresses this requirement |
| 🟡 **Covered (Proposed)** | An ADR addresses it, but that ADR is still `Proposed` |
| ⚠️ **Partial** | An ADR partially covers this, or coverage is ambiguous |
| ❌ **Gap** | No ADR addresses this requirement |
| ❓ **Not assessed** | The ADR is unreadable, or has no `## Status` section |

> **Read each ADR's `## Status` before marking coverage — an unaccepted decision
> is not coverage.** If `✅` meant only that *an ADR addresses this*, with no
> status qualification, a requirement covered entirely by `Proposed` ADRs would
> count as covered and this review could return **PASS: All requirements
> covered** over an architecture nobody had accepted. Four skills downstream
> (`create-control-manifest`, `create-epics`, `create-stories`, `gate-check`)
> require `Accepted`, so a PASS on that basis sends work forward that every one
> of them will refuse.
>
> `🟡` is **not** a pass state: it caps the verdict at **CONCERNS**, and names the
> route out — `/architecture-decision accept ADR-NNNN`. That route is the only
> thing that moves an ADR to `Accepted`; without it, grading `Proposed` as
> covered would be the only option, which is why it must never be graded so.

Build the full matrix:

```
## Traceability Matrix

| Requirement ID | GDD | System | Requirement | ADR Coverage | Status |
|---------------|-----|--------|-------------|--------------|--------|
| TR-combat-001 | combat.md | Combat | Hitbox detection < 1 frame | ADR-0003 | ✅ |
| TR-combat-002 | combat.md | Combat | Combo window timing | — | ❌ GAP |
| TR-inventory-001 | inventory.md | Inventory | Persistent item storage | ADR-0005 | ✅ |
```

Count the totals: X covered, Y partial, Z gaps.

---

## Phase 3b: Story and Test Linkage (RTM mode only)

*Skip this phase unless the argument is `rtm` or `full` with stories present.*

This phase extends the Phase 3 matrix to include the story that implements
each requirement and the test that verifies it — producing the full
Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM).

### Step 3b-1 — Load stories

Glob `production/epics/**/*.md` (excluding EPIC.md index files) to establish the
denominator. Then collect the fields with **targeted section greps, not a full
read of each story** — the same two-grep form `/test-evidence-review` uses for
this identical extraction:

```
Grep pattern="## Test Evidence" glob="production/epics/**/story-*.md" output_mode="content" -A 8
Grep pattern="TR-" glob="production/epics/**/story-*.md" output_mode="content"
```

- **TR-ID** — from the second grep.
- **Test file path** — under `## Test Evidence`, captured by the first grep's `-A 8`.
- **Status** — from the story header; add `Grep pattern="^> \*\*Status\*\*"` if not already captured.
- **Story path and title** — from the file name and path; no read at all.

Full-read a story only when its Test Evidence section is missing or ambiguous.

### Step 3b-2 — Load test files

Glob the engine's test root (`.claude/docs/directory-structure.md`): Godot
`tests/unit/**/*_test.*` and `tests/integration/**/*_test.*`; Unity
`Assets/Tests/**/*Tests.cs`; Unreal `Source/*/Private/Tests/**/*.cpp`. With no
engine configured, say the test index could not be built rather than reading an
empty glob as "no tests". Build an index: system → [test file paths].

For each test file path from Step 3b-1, confirm via Glob whether the file
actually exists. Note MISSING if the stated path does not exist.

### Step 3b-3 — Build the extended RTM

For each TR-ID in the Phase 3 matrix, add:
- **Story**: the story file path(s) that reference this TR-ID (may be multiple)
- **Test File**: the test file path stated in the story's Test Evidence section
- **Test Status**: COVERED (test file exists) / MISSING (path stated but not
  found) / NONE (no test path stated, story type may be Visual/Feel/UI) /
  NO STORY (requirement has no story yet — pre-production gap)

Extended matrix format:

```
## Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)

| TR-ID | GDD | Requirement | ADR | Story | Test File | Test Status |
|-------|-----|-------------|-----|-------|-----------|-------------|
| TR-combat-001 | combat.md | Hitbox < 1 frame | ADR-0003 | story-001-hitbox.md | tests/unit/combat/hitbox_test.gd | COVERED |
| TR-combat-002 | combat.md | Combo window | — | story-002-combo.md | — | NONE (Visual/Feel) |
| TR-inventory-001 | inventory.md | Persistent storage | ADR-0005 | — | — | NO STORY |
```

RTM coverage summary:
- COVERED: [N] — requirements with ADR + story + passing test
- MISSING test: [N] — story exists but test file not found
- NO STORY: [N] — requirements with ADR but no story yet
- NO ADR: [N] — requirements without architectural coverage (from Phase 3 gaps)
- Full chain complete (COVERED): [N/total] ([%])

---
# /architecture-review — Phase 4: Cross-ADR Conflict Detection

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 4: Cross-ADR Conflict Detection

Compare every ADR against every other ADR to detect contradictions. A conflict
exists when:

- **Data ownership conflict**: Two ADRs claim exclusive ownership of the same data
- **Integration contract conflict**: ADR-A assumes System X has interface Y, but
  ADR-B defines System X with a different interface
- **Performance budget conflict**: ADR-A allocates N ms to physics, ADR-B allocates
  N ms to AI, together they exceed the total frame budget
- **Dependency cycle**: ADR-A says System X initialises before Y; ADR-B says Y
  initialises before X
- **Architecture pattern conflict**: ADR-A uses event-driven communication for a
  subsystem; ADR-B uses direct function calls to the same subsystem
- **State management conflict**: Two ADRs define authority over the same game state
  (e.g. both Combat ADR and Character ADR claim to own the health value)

For each conflict found:

```
## Conflict: [ADR-NNNN] vs [ADR-MMMM]
Type: [Data ownership / Integration / Performance / Dependency / Pattern / State]
ADR-NNNN claims: [...]
ADR-MMMM claims: [...]
Impact: [What breaks if both are implemented as written]
Resolution options:
  1. [Option A]
  2. [Option B]
```

### ADR Dependency Ordering

After conflict detection, analyse the dependency graph across all ADRs.

**Build the graph deterministically — do not trace it by hand:**

```
Bash: bash .claude/scripts/adr-dep-graph.sh
```

It collects every `Depends On` edge, runs Kahn's algorithm, and emits
`ADRS:` / `EDGES:` / `NO_DEPS_SECTION:` / `CYCLE:`. A model tracing A→B→C→A across
a dozen ADRs eventually misses an edge; the algorithm cannot. It reports
observations, not a verdict — you apply the meaning below.

**`NO_DEPS_SECTION` is load-bearing**: it makes "no cycles because the graph is
clean" distinguishable from "no cycles because half the ADRs declare no
dependencies". Report the second case as a structural gap, never as a clean graph.

Then interpret:

1. **Topological sort**: the emitted order — ADRs with no
   dependencies come first (Foundation), ADRs that depend on those come next, etc.
2. **Flag unresolved dependencies**: cross the `EDGES:` list against the `## Status`
   values already scanned in Phase 1b. If ADR-A depends on an ADR that is still
   `Proposed` or does not exist, flag it:
   ```
   ⚠️  ADR-0005 depends on ADR-0002 — but ADR-0002 is still Proposed.
       ADR-0005 cannot be safely implemented until ADR-0002 is Accepted.
   ```
3. **Cycle detection**: every `CYCLE:` line the script emitted is a
   `DEPENDENCY CYCLE` — report each one. Do not re-derive them by hand:
   ```
   🔴 DEPENDENCY CYCLE: ADR-0003 → ADR-0006 → ADR-0003
      This cycle must be broken before either can be implemented.
   ```
4. **Output recommended implementation order**:
   ```
   ### Recommended ADR Implementation Order (topologically sorted)
   Foundation (no dependencies):
     1. ADR-0001: [title]
     2. ADR-0003: [title]
   Depends on Foundation:
     3. ADR-0002: [title] (requires ADR-0001)
     4. ADR-0005: [title] (requires ADR-0003)
   Feature layer:
     5. ADR-0004: [title] (requires ADR-0002, ADR-0005)
   ```

# /architecture-review — Phases 5 and 5b: Engine Cross-Check and Design Revision Flags

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 5: Engine Compatibility Cross-Check

**In this file:**

- Version Consistency
- Post-Cutoff API Consistency
- Deprecated API Check
- Missing Engine Compatibility Sections
- Engine Specialist Consultation

Across all ADRs, check for engine consistency:

### Version Consistency
- Do all ADRs that mention an engine version agree on the same version?
- If any ADR was written for an older engine version, flag it as potentially stale

### Post-Cutoff API Consistency
- Collect all "Post-Cutoff APIs Used" fields from all ADRs
- For each, verify against the relevant module reference doc
- Check that no two ADRs make contradictory assumptions about the same post-cutoff API

### Deprecated API Check
- Grep all ADRs for API names listed in `deprecated-apis.md`
- Flag any ADR referencing a deprecated API

### Missing Engine Compatibility Sections
- List all ADRs that are missing the Engine Compatibility section entirely
- These are blind spots — their engine assumptions are unknown

Output format:
```
### Engine Audit Results
Engine: [name + version]
ADRs with Engine Compatibility section: X / Y total

Deprecated API References:
  - ADR-0002: uses [deprecated API] — deprecated since [version]

Stale Version References:
  - ADR-0001: written for [older version] — current project version is [version]

Post-Cutoff API Conflicts:
  - ADR-0004 and ADR-0007 both use [API] with incompatible assumptions
```

---

### Engine Specialist Consultation

After completing the engine audit above, spawn the **primary engine specialist** via `Agent` for a domain-expert second opinion:

=== docs/architecture/adr-0001-kernel-tick-driver-and-frame-order.md
# ADR-0001: Kernel Tick Driver and Frame Order

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-28

## Last Verified
2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-1a, D.5 and `docs/engine-reference/godot/` 4.7). Engine behaviours marked UNVERIFIED below have not been run on 4.7.2.

## Decision Makers
User (delegated all remaining design calls, 2026-10-28); Claude (author); reviewed by godot-specialist (engine: no blocking issues) and technical-director (TD-ADR: CONCERNS, amendments A1-A6, B7-B8 and C9-C13 applied in this revision).

## Summary
The simulation kernel needs exactly one clock, and three approved design documents still describe two different ones (the kernel's `_process`-driven `TickDriver`, and an older physics-callback tick). This ADR fixes the kernel's source: one `TickDriver` driven from the `_process` of a single always-processing host node, with a fixed per-frame order set by named process-priority constants, `tick_alpha` as the only value presentation reads from the clock, and the kernel's services handed to each module as a narrow injected facet rather than through an autoload.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (frame loop, node processing order), with an Input boundary |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. Every API used predates the 4.3 cutoff, but the pinned engine reference is silent on cross-node `process_priority` order and on how `Engine.time_scale` scales `_process(delta)`, and 4.7 changed input device IDs. |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 → 4.7 GDScript and Input rows), `deprecated-apis.md`, `current-best-practices.md`, `modules/input.md`, `modules/physics.md` |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None. `Node._process`, `Node.process_priority`, `Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, `RefCounted`, `Engine.time_scale` and `roundi()` all exist in 4.3. |
| **Verification Required** | (1) Spike KRN-LAT-02: with the Input Adapter, the host node and a presentation node in one scene, the recorded `_process` call order is adapter → driver → presentation, on a dev build and on a release export. (2) `Engine.time_scale` scaling of `delta` (the kernel GDD marks it UNVERIFIED). (3) The first-frame `delta` after a long block (scene load, window drag, focus loss, a debugger breakpoint) is finite and handled by the cap and forgiveness, not a crash; the boundary service discards the first frame after a load (CR-1a). (3a) Delta jitter at `physics_jitter_fix` 0.5 versus 0, with `application/run/delta_smoothing` on and off, and the cost of the empty 60 Hz physics tick in an empty-scene baseline; the decision is to leave all three at engine defaults and record the measured effect on the 0-tick/2-tick frame pattern and on latency, not to claim they have nothing to do with the tick (MainTimerSync may adjust the idle step as well as the physics step, UNVERIFIED). (3b) `_input` and `_unhandled_input` are delivered before the frame's `_process` calls (UNVERIFIED in the reference), checked in the same scene as KRN-LAT-02. (4) `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` fires after every `_process` in the frame (owned by ADR-0008; recorded here because the camera write depends on this order). |

## ADR Dependencies

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Depends On** | None (first ADR). The design source is `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-1, CR-1a and D.5. |
| **Enables** | ADR-0002 (command pipeline), ADR-0003 (block registry and hooks), ADR-0004 (notification and `tick_alpha` consumers), ADR-0006 (Save/Load boundary service timing), ADR-0008 (render pipeline: `present_time`, camera write), ADR-0009 (presentation subscriber contract), ADR-0019 (Input Adapter placement) |
| **Blocks** | Every epic that submits commands or draws from the clock: Player Controller, Pixel-Perfect Pipeline, Suit, Modular Ship Assembly (stories that quote the tick source), Interaction, Lighting. |
| **Ordering Note** | Do not **Accept** until the stale tick-source text is fixed in four GDDs and two architecture artifacts (see § GDD sync), spike KRN-LAT-02 has run (it now also checks `_input` delivery order and `time_scale`), and the TD-ADR amendments recorded below have been re-reviewed. If the spike fails, the sequential-parent fallback changes the Decision and the ADR needs a revision, not just a status change. Authoring now is safe because this ADR follows the kernel GDD (the owner), not the stale consumers. |

## GDD Requirements Addressed

| GDD System | Requirement | How This ADR Addresses It |
|------------|-------------|--------------------------|
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-1, CR-1a: fixed 60 Hz tick; `TickDriver` with injected delta driven from `_process` by one always-processing node; physics step is not the clock (TR-cmd-001, TR-cmd-002) | Decision § 1 adopts it verbatim and names the host node and the one `delta` conversion |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-1a priority table: input adapter, then driver, then presentation, with a lint on `process_priority` (TR-cmd-004) | Decision § 2 fixes the constants and the three lint rules |
| command-simulation-layer.md | D.5: lag dropped at end of frame, accumulator cleared on every transition into `RUNNING` (TR-cmd-003) | Decision § 1 and § 6 reference it; the `tick_alpha` derivation in § 4 depends on its remainder rule |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-1a main thread only; no `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` or `call_deferred` into kernel code (TR-cmd-005) | Implementation Guidelines; Alternative 3 rejected |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-2: per-tick phases P0–P6 (TR-cmd-006) | Architecture Diagram shows where the phases sit in the frame |
| player-controller-input.md | PC-1(a), PC-15: the Adapter samples and submits before the kernel steps; one tick latency (TR-pc-004) | Decision § 3: Adapter samples in its own `_process` at `INPUT_ADAPTER`; the GDD's "physics callback" wording is stale (§ GDD sync) |
| pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md | PR-9 (`present_time`), the interpolation formula in Section D, and the tick-driver routing at L227 / L297 / Open Question 10: sim stays 60 Hz at any render rate; tick-before-render ordering; tick-driver ownership (TR-pxl-021, TR-pxl-022) | Decision § 1, § 4 and § 6; the `physics_jitter_fix` / `max_physics_steps_per_frame` clauses are removed by the GDD fix |
| 2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md | LO-4: kernel clock for what the sim also computes, `present_time` for cosmetic phase (TR-light-008) | Decision § 4 records the rule |
| hud-and-suit-layer.md, chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md | Presentation reads committed state at render rate and never causes a tick (TR-hud-010, TR-charttable-005) | Decision § 4 and the Architecture Diagram |
| derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md | P3 budget wording tied to the frame step (TR-derelict-021) | The tick loop is the one place P3 cost is incurred; `STEP_BUDGET_MS` semantics are already settled by the owner (a 4 ms alarm threshold; the P3 target is 2.0 ms P99) and ADR-0003 records them, so IC-4 in the architecture document moves to ADR-0003 |

## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: The driver itself is an integer add, a divide and a loop; it is negligible against the kernel's budgets (P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99; frame simulation ≤ 4.0 ms for one tick and ≤ 6.0 ms for four), which are measured on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK. At 30 fps (RM-DECK) a frame normally runs two ticks; the 4-tick cap means slow motion begins below 15 fps.
- **Memory**: One `TickDriver`, one `KernelHost` node, a few integers. No per-frame allocation in the driver (`TickFrameResult` is reused).
- **Load Time**: None. The accumulator is cleared when load finishes, so load time is not repaid as ticks.
- **Network**: None at MVP. In VS-B a MIRROR kernel uses the same driver with no authority over commands (ADR-0002, ADR-0032).

## GDD sync (stale tick-source text)
**Status 2026-10-28: the consumer GDD passages below are corrected** (player-controller-input, suit-and-equipment, pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera, modular-ship-assembly); `tr-baseline.md` and `architecture.md` were corrected with this ADR. Acceptance still waits on spike KRN-LAT-02 and the TD-ADR re-review. The list records what was stale:
The kernel GDD (owner) is correct. These consumer passages still describe the physics callback and conflict with this ADR:
- `design/gdd/player-controller-input.md` L62 (PC-1(a)), L740 and L751 (latency terms), L1021 (Immediacy), L1077 (AC-PCI-003: "in the same physics callback")
- `design/gdd/suit-and-equipment.md` L1441
- `docs/architecture/tr-baseline.md` TR-pc-004 and TR-pxl-022 (stale requirement text that stories would embed; corrected in the same pass as this ADR)
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` § Data Flow 1 (priority values and the boundary-service-before-add order), OQ-1, OQ-13 and the paragraph that defers kernel access to ADR-0001 (corrected in the same pass)
- `design/gdd/pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md` L227, L297, L1219 (`physics_jitter_fix`, `max_physics_steps_per_frame`, "two accumulators")
- `design/gdd/modular-ship-assembly.md` L1058, L1161, L1528, L1593, L1772, L1940 (the "when the tick is driven by the physics callback" conditions, the boot assertion, and open item 41)

=== docs/architecture/adr-0002-authority-model-and-command-pipeline.md
# ADR-0002: Authority Model and Command Pipeline

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-28

## Last Verified
2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-4 to CR-7, CR-15 to CR-17 and `docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/networking.md`). No code exists yet; nothing here has been run on 4.7.2.

## Decision Makers
User (delegated all remaining design calls, 2026-10-28); Claude (author); reviewed by godot-specialist (engine: 3 blocking and 16 minor items, all applied in this revision) and technical-director (TD-ADR: CONCERNS; findings 1-10 applied in this revision). Amended the same day for ADR-0003's TD review: result and control-outcome handlers are kernel-invoked callables with the `(record, ctx: NotifyContext) -> CompletionToken` shape, and `register_command` lives on the `BlockRegistrar`.

## Summary
Every change to the simulation must enter as an authority-checked, plain-data command that the kernel stamps and orders, even in single-player where the one local player is the host. This ADR fixes how: capability handles (not globals) are the only way to submit or to call the control plane, a single ingress function stamps every command, each command type declares a payload schema the kernel enforces, and ownership is judged by a kernel-held binding table keyed by a stable PlayerId rather than by network peer id.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (command ingress and authority), with a Networking boundary kept dormant until VS-B |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. Nothing used here is post-cutoff, but `var_to_bytes` size behaviour for payload checks, `Variant.Type` coverage and the 4.7 peer-id behaviour of `MultiplayerAPI` are not covered by the pinned reference. |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 → 4.7 GDScript and Core rows), `deprecated-apis.md`, `modules/networking.md`, `modules/input.md` |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None in the MVP. Typed `Dictionary[K, V]` (4.4) is allowed inside the kernel but never at the payload boundary, where payloads are untyped `Dictionary` so the whitelist can inspect them. |
| **Verification Required** | (1) `var_to_bytes(payload, false).size()` is cheap enough at the admitted command rates and is a pure function of the payload's value (it is used only as a threshold; never as hash input, because the encoder's size choices for ints and floats are not a byte-stable cross-platform contract, UNVERIFIED). (2) A `Dictionary` or `Array` payload that contains itself is stopped by the depth cap (the walk recurses to depth 9 and rejects) **before** any serialisation is attempted; serialising a cyclic container is not assumed safe. (2a) A wide payload cannot burn time before the size check: the walk aborts as soon as a running upper-bound byte estimate exceeds `MAX_PAYLOAD`. (3) The peer id a `MultiplayerAPI` RPC reports for the host is `1` on 4.7.2 (VS-B only; recorded here because `HOST_PEER_ID` = 1 is baked into the binding table). (4) GDScript has no private constructors, so "only the kernel builds a `Command`" is enforced at run time (a `_sealed` flag and a ring-slot check) and also by a CI lint that greps for `Command.new()`. (5) `Callable.is_valid()` is false for a method Callable whose target object was freed, and `Callable.call()` on a freed target errors rather than skips (UNVERIFIED; both from memory). (6) Writing into a `PackedInt64Array` fetched from a `Dictionary` value mutates the stored array only through an explicit read-modify-write (UNVERIFIED across versions); the binding table avoids the question. |

## ADR Dependencies

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Depends On** | ADR-0001 (the injected-kernel rule and the frame order this ADR relies on; **Proposed**, not yet Accepted) |
| **Enables** | ADR-0003 (block registry uses the command-type descriptor defined here), ADR-0016 (binding-table rebuild on restore), ADR-0019 (Input Adapter uses a surface handle), ADR-0020/0021/0022/0026/0027 (each registers command types against this contract), ADR-0030 (`PauseGate` uses a control handle), ADR-0032 (remote ingress for VS-B) |
| **Blocks** | Every story that registers or submits a command type: Player Controller, Interaction, Suit, Emitter toggles, Assembly, Web Map, Chart Table pause. |
| **Ordering Note** | Scope edge with ADR-0003: this ADR owns the **meaning** of the command fields, the ingress and the control-plane API; ADR-0003 owns the **registration descriptors**, the owner-callable contract and the kernel state machine. The `payload_schema` field defined here is added to ADR-0003's `CommandTypeDescriptor`. The kernel GDD's CR-6 field list does not name `payload_schema`; see § GDD sync. |

## GDD Requirements Addressed

| GDD System | Requirement | How This ADR Addresses It |
|------------|-------------|--------------------------|
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-4: commands are plain data stamped by the kernel (`issuer_peer`, `origin`, `seq`, `submission_id`), never payload-borne; no constructor without `issuer_peer` (TR-cmd-008) | § 2: only `_admit` builds and fills a `Command`; lint forbids `Command.new()` elsewhere |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-5: `submit()` is fire-and-forget; exactly one terminal result per command, flushed at P5 and once per frame (TR-cmd-009) | § 2 and § 7 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-4 payload whitelist and `MAX_PAYLOAD` (TR-cmd-010) | § 2 order of checks; § 3 adds per-type shape and range on top |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-7: origin and actor-binding authority check at P2; single-player is host peer 1 → PlayerId 1 (TR-cmd-012) | § 4 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-7, CR-18: the kernel rebuilds binding half (b) on every `LOADING` pass (TR-cmd-013) | § 4 states the data structure; the rebuild order is ADR-0016 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-13: apply order ascending `(queued_tick, host_order)`; identical stream gives identical hash (TR-cmd-027) | § 5; hashing is ADR-0005 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-15: control plane is host-local, served at the next boundary in arrival order (TR-cmd-028) | § 6 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-16: pause is single-player only; only `allowed_when_paused` types, non-gameplay blocks (TR-cmd-030) | § 6 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-17: queue, per-issuer and payload bounds are boot assertions; `QUEUE_FULL`, never a silent drop (TR-cmd-031) | § 5 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | HOST/MIRROR share an identical public API (TR-cmd-034, API identity only; the block-descriptor `repl_hint` field is ADR-0003) | § 8; replication shape is ADR-0032 |
| player-controller-input.md | PC command authority: a command whose issuer does not own the actor is `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)`; opaque `correlation` echoed to the caller (TR-pc-024) | § 4 and § 7 |
| interaction-system.md | IA-40: while paused no diegetic verb is admitted (`PAUSED`, never queued) (TR-interact-029) | § 6 |
| chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md | `PauseGate` is the single adapter to the control plane and re-issues the desired pause state until the kernel matches (TR-charttable-003, TR-charttable-004) | § 1 (control handle) and § 6 |
| sanity-and-hallucination-rules.md, suit-and-equipment.md, interaction-system.md | Persistent per-player state keyed by PlayerId, never peer id | § 4; Implementation Guidelines |

## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: Admission is O(1) per submit apart from the payload walk (bounded by 4 KiB and depth 8) and, for coalescing types only, a scan of at most 1,024 slots. At the admitted rates (a few tens of commands per second) this is far inside the kernel's budgets (frame simulation ≤ 4.0 ms P99; P3 ≤ 2.0 ms), measured on release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK. The P2 ownership check is a scan of a few `int64`s.
- **Memory**: The queue ring is preallocated (`QUEUE_CAPACITY` slots); the joint queue and command-log bound is a boot assertion against `COMMAND_MEMORY_BUDGET` (16 MiB). One `Command` object per admitted submit (allocated, not pooled); `PackedInt64Array`s for the binding table.
- **Load Time**: Rebuilding binding half (b) on `LOADING` is O(players × entities) and runs inside the existing atomic boundary service.
- **Network**: None at MVP. The remote ingress adapter and rate limiting (`REMOTE_RATE_LIMIT`, `RATE_WINDOW_TICKS`) are VS-B.

## GDD sync
**Status 2026-10-28: the five kernel-GDD items below are applied** to `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` (CR-4, CR-5, CR-6, CR-7, CR-15 and the States and Transitions sentence). The per-command-owner item stays open by design: each owner lists its `payload_schema` when its stories are written. Acceptance still waits on the review noted in the Ordering Note. What was needed:
- `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-6 (registration field list) and CR-4: add the mandatory `payload_schema` field (shape and range only). Owner GDD, so this ADR's addition becomes the spec.
- `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-4 / CR-10: record that `submit_system` is exposed on `HookContext`/`ApplyContext` and the test ingress, not as a free function, and that submit rights are capability handles issued in `BOOTING`.
- `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-5: record the **normative admission order** in § Admission above (type resolved before the kernel-state check; capacity after coalescing).
- `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-7 and CR-15: name `request_bind_seat` / `request_unbind_seat` as the host-only writers of binding half (a); and amend the States and Transitions sentence "control-plane requests have none" to say outcomes are delivered to the requester's outcome handler in a list separate from the CR-5 command result buffer.
- `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-5/CR-16: the queue-flush `Dropped(...)` results on entry to `LOADING`, `SHUTTING_DOWN` and `FAULTED` are already there; state that superseded tombstones free capacity.
- Per-command owners (Controller, Interaction, Suit, Emitter, Assembly, Web Map, Sanity) list each command's `payload_schema` in their GDD when their stories are written (ADR-0020, -0021, -0026, -0027, -0019).

=== docs/architecture/adr-0003-state-block-registry-and-owner-contract.md
# ADR-0003: State-Block Registry, Write Discipline and Owner-Callable Contract

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-28

## Last Verified
2026-10-28 (against `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` CR-2, CR-3, CR-6, CR-8, CR-9, CR-12, CR-14, CR-18, CR-19 and States and Transitions, and `docs/engine-reference/godot/breaking-changes.md` and `current-best-practices.md` 4.5–4.7). No code exists; nothing here has been run on 4.7.2.

## Decision Makers
User (delegated all remaining design calls, 2026-10-28); Claude (author). Reviewed by godot-specialist (engine: design idiomatic and implementable; three verification and wording items and twelve minor notes, all applied) and technical-director (TD-ADR: CONCERNS; finding A1 and amendments B1–B11, C and E applied in this revision).

## Summary
About fifteen systems register state blocks, step hooks and command handlers with the kernel, and the kernel must call them, check that they finished, and let them write only inside a kernel-issued scope. This ADR fixes that contract in GDScript: owners are plain objects that register typed `Callable`s (no base class), every kernel call receives a reused context and ends in `return ctx.complete()`, all writes and dirty marks go through a reused `WriteScope` (including during new-game construction), faults are integers with static per-system domains, hooks run from a precomputed schedule, and the kernel state machine is a data table that generates its own test.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (scripting contracts, callable invocation) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | HIGH for the owner-callable contract. 4.7 made an override of a typed-return method inherit the return type (it needs an explicit `return`) and stopped packed-array element writes from calling the property setter; both bear on this contract (confirmed in `breaking-changes.md`). What `Callable.call()` returns after the callee aborts on a runtime error is documented only in the kernel GDD (CR-19), not in the pinned engine reference. |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`, `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 → 4.7 GDScript rows), `deprecated-apis.md`, `current-best-practices.md` (GDScript 4.5+ and 4.7: `@abstract`, typed-return override rule, packed-array element writes, lambda capture by value, release-build script backtracing) |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | None required. `@abstract` (4.5) is deliberately not used. The 4.7 packed-array element-write change is avoided by marking dirty keys explicitly in mutators. `Callable.get_argument_count()` is used for a boot-time signature check if it exists on 4.7.2 (UNVERIFIED; otherwise the check is skipped and the token check covers it). |
| **Verification Required** | (1) **Gates acceptance.** On a **release export**, a registered owner `Callable` typed `-> CompletionToken` that aborts on a script error returns something that is not the armed token, so `INCOMPLETE` is detected; and a typed function with a path that never reaches `return` is rejected at parse time ("not all code paths return a value"). Both are UNVERIFIED against the reference and are proved by KRN-CTX-06. (2) `assert()` is stripped in release; a lint plus test (1) prove no control flow depends on it. (3) A `Callable` bound to a `RefCounted` method keeps the object alive (UNVERIFIED), which the teardown rule assumes. (4) Packed-array copy semantics for the schedule and dirty set (S0-a). (5) `Callable.call()` cost with a context argument at the worst-case calls per tick (15 hooks plus the command batch) fits the P3 budget, and `PackedInt32Array` element reads allocate nothing (S1). |

## ADR Dependencies

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Depends On** | ADR-0001 (injected facets, frame order; Proposed), ADR-0002 (command-type descriptor meaning, handles; Proposed) |
| **Enables** | ADR-0004 (notification consumes the dirty keys collected here), ADR-0005 (canonical encode and hash through `snapshot`), ADR-0006 (snapshot and restore callables), ADR-0016 (restore ordering; consumes `restore_after`), ADR-0031 (diagnostics channel descriptor), and every system ADR that registers a block or hook (ADR-0011, 0013, 0015, 0017, 0019, 0020 to 0027) |
| **Blocks** | Every story that registers a block, hook or command type. |
| **Ordering Note** | Scope edge with ADR-0002: ADR-0002 owns command-field meaning, ingress and the control plane; **this ADR states the complete `CommandTypeDescriptor`** and moves `register_command` onto the `BlockRegistrar` (ADR-0002 is amended to match, together with its result-handler signature, finding B5). Scope edge with ADR-0004: the dirty key is an opaque `int` here; ADR-0004 fixes its layout. The kernel GDD needs amendments listed in § GDD sync (epoch token; `FAULTED` re-entry qualifier; long-lived read views; fault-code table). |

## GDD Requirements Addressed

| GDD System | Requirement | How This ADR Addresses It |
|------------|-------------|--------------------------|
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-3: hooks topologically sorted; cycle or unknown id fails boot; stale-edge warning (TR-cmd-007) | § 8 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-6: registration only in `BOOTING`, frozen after; no silent defaults (TR-cmd-011) | §§ 2, 8; Guidelines |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-8: single-owner blocks with the full descriptor; PlayerId-keyed persistent state (TR-cmd-014) | § 2 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-8: ids block-local; cross-block references keyed `(block_id, entity_id)` (TR-cmd-015) | § 2, with ADR-0002 for the binding table |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-9: writes only by owner mutators inside a `WriteScope`; refused elsewhere; validate-then-apply, fault on defect (TR-cmd-021) | §§ 4, 5 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-18: `init_world` steps run under one `WriteScope` before `post_restore` | § 4 (`INIT` phase) |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-19(a)(b): ctx, `return ctx.complete()`, completion sentinel (TR-cmd-022) | § 3 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | CR-12: read views are getter-only facades; `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` (TR-cmd-026) | § 7 |
| command-simulation-layer.md | States and Transitions: seven states (TR-cmd-029) | § 9 |
| emitter, player-controller-input, interaction, suit, ship-section-and-layout, ship-body, web-map, attention, horror, sanity GDDs | Each registers its block with `persist`/`persist_scope`/`scope`/`repl_hint`/`restore_after` and its hooks with divisor, offset and `after` (TR-emitter-001, TR-pc-002, TR-pc-005, TR-interact-014, TR-suit-001, TR-section-001, TR-shipbody-005, TR-shipbody-011, TR-webmap-002, TR-attention-001, TR-horror-001, TR-sanity-001) | §§ 2, 8 |
| player-controller-input.md, modular-ship-assembly.md | Every kernel-invoked callable receives `ctx` and ends in `return ctx.complete()` (TR-pc-019, TR-assembly-008) | § 3 |
| modular-ship-assembly.md | `assembly.state` SIM block with a four-block `restore_after` (TR-assembly-011) | § 2 |
| chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md | Settings and menu state registers as a non-`gameplay` block (TR-charttable-023) | § 2 (`gameplay`) |

## Performance Implications
- **CPU**: One `Callable.call()` per due hook and per dispatched command, selected by one schedule lookup. The MVP's 15 hooks at divisors 1, 5, 6 and 12 average well under 15 due per tick. Re-arming a context or scope is a handful of field writes. P3 ≤ 2.0 ms P99 with a 4 ms alarm, measured on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (spike S1).
- **Memory**: The schedule is `C` (60) small `PackedInt32Array`s built once; one context per kind, one token per context and the scope objects are allocated at boot. No per-tick kernel allocation in a quiet tick.
- **Load Time**: Registration, validation and the hook sort run once; facades are built once at the freeze.
- **Network**: None. `repl_hint` is stored now and consumed in VS-B (ADR-0032).

## GDD sync
**Status 2026-10-28: all six items below are applied** to `design/gdd/command-simulation-layer.md` (CR-8, CR-18, CR-19, the States and Transitions rows, Tuning Knobs), `derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md` and `web-map-and-transit.md`. - CR-18: `init_world(world_seed, scope, ctx)` receives the shared `INIT` scope; dirty keys from `INIT`/`RESTORE` scopes are replaced by one `ALL` batch per block on `LOADING → RUNNING`.
- States and Transitions, the `RUNNING / PAUSED / FAULTED request_new_game` row and the `FAULTED request_restore / request_new_game` row: "legal only when the registries validated (`registry_valid`); a boot-failure `FAULTED` exits only to `SHUTTING_DOWN`" (closes OQ-5). Add bind/unbind as non-transition requests.
- Add the static fault-domain table, the kernel fault codes, the violation set and `MAX_SCHEDULE_CYCLE_TICKS` (Tuning Knobs).
- `design/gdd/derelict-authoring-handmade-kits.md` (TR-derelict-021), `design/gdd/web-map-and-transit.md` (TR-webmap-025): `STEP_BUDGET_MS` is an alarm threshold; the P3 target is 2.0 ms P99 (IC-4).

## Required ADRs

Thirty-four decisions. Numbers are sequential; the GDD-named candidates each one absorbs are in brackets, so `/architecture-decision` can find the anchors. Several GDD candidates were the same decision under two names and are merged: ADR-LAY-03 and ADR-BODY-03 (scene projection); ADR-BODY-04 and the kernel tick ADR (tick source); ADR-LAY-02 and Emitter candidate 4 (OccluderSource); ADR-LAY-07 belongs to the kernel restore order. **v2 changes:** ADR-0009 is split so the subscriber contract every presentation system needs is Foundation while the Y-sort scene shape (gated by SP-YSORT-1) becomes Core ADR-0034; ADR-0018 folds into ADR-0028 if the lighting spike settles both at once; ADR-0006, ADR-0007 and ADR-0024 carry 64-65 requirements each and are written as sectioned ADRs with one numbered sub-decision per section (container / versioning / restore epoch; content pipeline / boot lints / ids; isolation / Filter query / truth-channel tags) so each part can be reviewed on its own.

### Must have before coding starts (Foundation)

| ADR | Title | Absorbs | Decides |
|---|---|---|---|
| ADR-0001 | Kernel tick driver and frame order | kernel tick ADR, ADR-BODY-04 | `_process` TickDriver, priority order, `tick_alpha`, `present_time`, where the Adapter samples input |

OQ-5) |
| ADR-0004 | Change notification and dirty keys | kernel OQ 8, ADR-LSG-06 | kernel observer registry vs signals (OQ-4), subscriber classes, int dirty keys, catch-up merge, a debug-build check that every changed block marked a dirty key |
| ADR-0005 | Determinism, keyed RNG, canonical encoding and hashing | kernel H64/mix64, ADR-LSG-07, K-1 | integer-only sim, `rng_derive(_epoch)`, TLV encoding, H64, cached block hashes, replay guarantees |
| ADR-0006 | Save container, generations, versioning and restore epoch | ADR-LSG-05, S-1, rulings R13/R14 | file container, ring, write protocol, worker thread, migration, 64-bit interchange, PROFILE split, `slot_epoch.bin` |
| ADR-0007 | Static content data pipeline and stable type IDs | ADR-LSG-08, ADR-LAY-04 | JSON under `assets/data/`, manifests, int-casting, immutable catalogs, append-only ids, boot lints, export filters |
| ADR-0008 | Render pipeline wiring and integer scaling | pipeline render-wiring ADR | SubViewport stack, k and H, RENDER_MODE, stretch pins, zoom by logical size, **renderer method (Forward+ vs Compatibility) and Windows driver (D3D12 vs Vulkan)**, the single draw-call budget table |

| ADR-0028 | 2D lighting budget and modifier chain | node pools, shadow slots, demotion, modifier chain, glow/HDR, trail budget, the shared frame-mean flash rule (IC-7), 4.7 line-drawing change for trails and hairlines |
| ADR-0029 | Audio architecture | bus tree, voice pool, `cue_requests()`, whether audio can lie |
| ADR-0030 | UI framework | HUD layout, Theme, dual focus, menus state machine, localisation keys, 4.7 line-drawing change for instrument needles, AccessKit recorded as deferred to Alpha |

| ADR | Title | When |
|---|---|---|

| ADR-0033 | Presentation-only debris physics | before VS (ADR-BODY-05) |

### Spikes that gate ADRs

| Spike | Gates | Source |
|---|---|---|
| S0-a / S0-b (packed-array alias semantics; `@warning_ignore_start("integer_division")`; signed 64-bit literal; arithmetic `>>` and the masking logical shifts need; H64 and `mix64` golden vectors) | ADR-0005, ADR-0010, ADR-0011 | life-support-graph |

| SP-YSORT-1 (Y-sort tie under reparent; per-body vs per-section TileMapLayer) | ADR-0034 | ship-section-and-layout-data-model |
| Pipeline spike step 11 (SubViewport wiring, RENDER_MODE A/B, `RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw` order against `process_priority`) | ADR-0008 | pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera |
| Lighting spike steps 1-10 (art bible 8.12; LO-10 shadow origin). **Its renderer method and driver result gates Foundation ADR-0008, so it runs before Foundation coding**, not with the Feature tier | ADR-0008, ADR-0018, ADR-0028 | 2d-lighting-and-occlusion |
| S1 / SP-ENG-1 (GDScript hot-path cost on an RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release export: a stub Graph with 12 phases, `emitter.place`, the P3 loop at realistic counts, **accessor and `Callable.call` overhead per ms**, four-tick catch-up; needs an exported benchmark harness outside gdUnit4) | ADR-0012, ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0017; decides the GDExtension rung | graph, layout, body, emitter |
| Weld property test (generated section pairs: `can_join` true implies all four apply steps return OK; verifier INV-1..INV-10 after each) | ADR-0021 | modular-ship-assembly |
| Save worker (`DirAccess.rename` over an existing file on Windows, including locked and antivirus-held targets; quit during a write with a bounded join; snapshot hitch size) | ADR-0006 | save-load-and-versioned-format |

**Spike order** (lead-programmer): S1 first, then the kernel skeleton (KRN-LAT-02), then S0-a/b, then the weld property test, then the save worker. result.output:
## Decision

### 1. The tick source is `_process`, in one host node

A single `KernelHost` node (`extends Node`, `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`) owns a `TickDriver` (`RefCounted`, no scene tree) and calls it from its own `_process(delta)`. The host does one thing with the engine's `delta`: it converts it once, `delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0))`, and passes the integer to the driver. That conversion and the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads **that reach the simulation** (kernel H9). Presentation keeps its own `_process(delta)` for `present_time`, camera smoothing and cosmetic accumulators (Pipeline PR-9; Chart Table CT-43) and may read the committed tick `T` where the sim also computes the value (for example `beacon_aim(T)`, LO-27); none of that feeds back into the simulation. The driver is exactly the one specified in kernel CR-1a and D.5: an integer accumulator in units of microseconds × `TICK_RATE` (`TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 per tick), a boundary service before any tick, `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)`, a re-read of the kernel state after every `step()`, lag forgiveness (`LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0), result flush, and the paused service. This ADR does not restate those rules; the GDD is their authority. It records the *placement* and *order* decisions below.

**The physics callback is not the clock and is not used by any simulation or presentation code in the MVP.** No script in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/` defines `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces`; `physics_interpolation` stays off. The kernel does not read `physics_jitter_fix`, `physics_ticks_per_second` or `max_physics_steps_per_frame`, and nothing is coupled to them, **but they can shape the `delta` the host receives** (the engine's main-loop timer sync produces both, UNVERIFIED), so the spike logs delta jitter at `physics_jitter_fix` 0.5 and at 0. Determinism does not depend on it, because replays inject `delta_us`. A boot check records `physics_ticks_per_second != TICK_RATE` in the diagnostics header as information, not as a failure. A later Vertical Slice physics projection (ADR-0033) runs in `_physics_process` as a read-only PROJECTOR and never steps the kernel.

### 2. Frame order is fixed by named priority constants

Godot runs `_process` in ascending `process_priority`, ties broken by tree order. Tree order is not a contract we want to depend on, so the order is fixed by three constants in one file, `src/kernel/process_priority.gd`:

```gdscript
class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted

## Lower values run first inside one rendered frame.
const INPUT_ADAPTER: int = -100   # INPUT_SURFACE objects only; samples input, calls submit()
const TICK_DRIVER: int = -50      # KernelHost: boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, result flush
const PRESENTATION: int = 0       # engine default; every presentation node, so a node that forgets to set it still runs after the driver
```

The three-step order is therefore **input adapter → tick driver → presentation**, matching the kernel GDD's priority table (its ordinals 0, 1 and 2 are order only; the values above are the implementation). Choosing `PRESENTATION` as the engine default is deliberate: an unset node lands after the driver, which is the safe failure.

Rules, each of which becomes a lint (ADR-0010):
- A node whose `process_priority` is below `TICK_DRIVER` must be a registered INPUT_SURFACE object. Nothing else may run before the driver. Scene files (`.tscn`) must not set `process_priority` at all (the Inspector stores a literal); code sets it from `ProcessPriority`. A regex cannot see priorities set at runtime, so the authoritative check is a **boot-time tree walk**: every node whose priority is below `TICK_DRIVER` is a registered INPUT_SURFACE object, only `KernelHost` uses `TICK_DRIVER`'s value, and every INPUT_SURFACE, `KernelHost` and presentation node has the default (main-thread) `process_thread_group`, because a sub-thread group leaves the main-thread ordering and breaks the main-thread rule. Exactly which rules the lint tool can enforce statically and which move to boot walks is ADR-0010's call (OQ-16).
- No node other than `KernelHost` may use `TICK_DRIVER`'s value.
- A presentation node's `process_priority` is `PRESENTATION` or greater and is never set to a literal; it references the constant.
- Code in `src/sim/` and `src/presentation/` does not `await get_tree().process_frame` (that signal fires outside the per-node ordering, UNVERIFIED); waiting is expressed in ticks or in `present_time`.

### 3. The Input Adapter samples and submits in its own `_process`

The Adapter (an INPUT_SURFACE, Player Controller GDD PC-1(a)) reads device state and calls `submit()` from its `_process` at `ProcessPriority.INPUT_ADAPTER`. It may latch raw events in `_input`/`_unhandled_input`, which the engine delivers before the frame's `_process` calls, but it submits only from `_process`. Its commands are therefore queued before the driver's boundary service and tick loop run, so an intent sampled in frame N sits in tick T's P1 batch, is applied in P2 and is integrated in P3 of the same tick: one tick of latency, never two. The Adapter never samples in `_physics_process`. Devices are identified by event type, not by `device == 0` (4.7 changed mouse and keyboard device IDs; ADR-0019).

In a frame that runs several ticks (catch-up), the Adapter has submitted once, so only the first tick of that frame sees new commands. Continuing movement survives because intent state lives in `controller.state` and commands are edge- or change-based, not per-tick.

### 4. `tick_alpha` is the only value presentation reads *from the driver*

At the end of each driver frame the driver publishes `tick_alpha = clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0.0, 1.0)` (identical to kernel D.3's `t_since_last_commit / tick_duration`; the casts are required, because `acc` and `TICK_UNITS` are both `int` and an unmarked `/` is integer division in GDScript, which would give 0 on every normal frame and fail the `integer_division` warning policy). It is a presentation-only float: it is not a state block, is never hashed or saved, and the simulation never reads it (kernel H9). Presentation reads it once per frame in its own `_process` and interpolates previous-to-current committed state with `pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) * tick_alpha)` (Pipeline Section D, interpolation formula; restore case in its Edge Cases). Because forgiveness at `LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS` = 0 drops whole lag ticks at the end of every frame but keeps the sub-tick remainder, `acc < TICK_UNITS` after the driver runs in `RUNNING`, so `tick_alpha` is continuous and in [0, 1). **Two rules from kernel D.3 are binding and are restated here because they are easy to lose:** (1) **while the kernel is not `RUNNING` the driver holds `tick_alpha` at 1.0**, so a paused, loading or saving game draws the latest committed pose and never a frozen partway-back pose; (2) **on every transition into `RUNNING` the kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every `interpolated` block** (ADR-0003), so `previous == current` on resume and the first running frame, including a 0-tick frame, cannot interpolate across a discontinuity.

Presentation also keeps a render-rate cosmetic clock, `present_time`, owned by the Pipeline root (Pipeline PR-9, ADR-0008). The rule recorded here: **cosmetic phase (flicker, gutter, fades) uses `present_time`; anything the simulation also computes (beacon aim, poses, wane) uses the kernel tick; the tick counter is never used for cosmetic phase** (Lighting LO-4).

### 5. The kernel reaches modules by injection

There is no `Kernel` autoload and no static singleton for kernel or game state. The main scene's root script (the **composition root**, `src/game/game.gd`) constructs the kernel, the `TickDriver` and the `KernelHost`, then gives every module and subscriber **the narrowest facet it needs through `setup()`**, never the whole `Kernel`: a simulation module receives the registration and mutator-scope services ADR-0003 defines; a presentation subscriber receives `subscribe(...)`, the read views and a read-only **`PresentationClock`** (`tick_alpha`, `T`, `running`, backed by the driver); and the right to submit or to call the control plane comes only from the named handles ADR-0002 defines, which the root issues to a few objects. Handing the whole kernel to presentation would give it `submit()`, which kernel CR-10 limits to INPUT_SURFACE. Headless tests construct their own kernel, driver and facets and need no scene. In the code examples in `docs/architecture/architecture.md`, `Kernel.` reads as "the injected facet". There are no recorded exceptions.

### 6. Pause, load and the tree

The kernel's `PAUSED` state is the only pause the simulation knows (kernel CR-16). `KernelHost` is `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`, so the driver keeps running its boundary service whether or not anything pauses the scene tree, and no simulation code reads `SceneTree.paused`. Whether the UI layers use `SceneTree.paused` or per-layer `process_mode` is **not decided here**: the Chart Table GDD routes it to its own ADR candidate (a) and the Debug Overlay GDD (E-DO-48, AC-DO-174) assumes `SceneTree.paused` can be true; ADR-0030 decides it, and it must keep `KernelHost` and the Input Adapter `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`. Window focus loss, an OS-level stall, a debugger break or a long load simply produces one large `delta`: the cap (`MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME` = 4) and forgiveness absorb it, and the accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`, so loads, saves and pauses never cause catch-up bursts afterwards (kernel CR-1a).

### Architecture Diagram

```
Engine main loop, one rendered frame (_process in ascending process_priority)
│
├─ -100  Input Adapter           [INPUT_SURFACE]   reads input → surface.submit(...)  (SurfaceHandle, ADR-0002)           (queued only)
│
├─  -50  KernelHost._process(delta)
│          delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta × 1e6))                  ← the only wall-clock read that reaches the sim
│          TickDriver.frame(delta_us):
│            1 boundary service (SAVING/LOADING/pause/resume; may clear acc, discard this frame's delta)
│            2 repeat ticks_run times, re-reading kernel state after each:
│                 Kernel.step() = P0 begin · P1 intake · P2 dispatch · P3 step hooks · P4 commit · P5 notify · P6 boundary
│            3 forgiveness (drop whole lag ticks, keep the sub-tick remainder)
│            4 flush the result buffer
│            5 if PAUSED: paused service
│          tick_alpha = clampf(float(acc) / float(TICK_UNITS), 0, 1)   (1.0 while not RUNNING)
│
└─   0   Presentation nodes      [PRESENTATION]    handlers already marked dirty at P5;
           (Pipeline root, Avatar Presenter, Lighting, Trail,        draw from committed views at tick_alpha;
            Instruments, HUD, Audio, Debug)                          Pipeline writes camera in frame_pre_draw

_physics_process: not used by the kernel, simulation or presentation in the MVP.
```

### Key Interfaces

```gdscript
class_name TickDriver extends RefCounted
## Turns an injected wall-time delta into whole kernel ticks. No scene tree, no engine clock.
func _init(kernel: Kernel, params: TickParams) -> void
func frame(delta_us: int) -> TickFrameResult   # boundary service, tick loop, forgiveness, flush; returns ticks_run, dropped, tick_alpha
var tick_alpha: float:                         # presentation-only; read once per frame
	get: return _tick_alpha

class_name KernelHost extends Node
func setup(driver: TickDriver) -> void         # called by the composition root; sets process_mode and process_priority
func _process(delta: float) -> void            # returns at once if setup() has not run (null driver); else delta_us = maxi(0, roundi(delta * 1_000_000.0)); driver.frame(delta_us)

class_name ProcessPriority extends RefCounted  # constants shown in Decision § 2

# Every module and subscriber:
func setup(facet: ModuleFacet) -> void         # the narrowest facet for the module's class (ADR-0003 / ADR-0009); stored; never looked up through a global

class_name PresentationClock extends RefCounted  # read-only, backed by the TickDriver
var tick_alpha: float:
	get: return _driver.tick_alpha                 # 1.0 while the kernel is not RUNNING
var T: int:
	get: return _kernel_clock_t()                  # last committed tick
var running: bool:
	get: return _kernel_running()
```

### Implementation Guidelines
- **Must** drive `Kernel.step()` only from `TickDriver.frame()`, and call `TickDriver.frame()` only from `KernelHost._process`. Tests may call either directly.
- **Must never** define `_physics_process` or `_integrate_forces` in `src/kernel/`, `src/sim/` or `src/presentation/`.
- **Must** use the `ProcessPriority` constants; **must never** write a literal `process_priority` value.
- **Must** submit input only from the Input Adapter's `_process`; **must never** call `submit()` from `_input`, `_physics_process` or a signal handler.
- **Must** pass each module its facet with `setup()`; **must never** add an autoload, a static variable or a group lookup that exposes the kernel, a block or a read view, and **must never** give a presentation node the whole `Kernel`.
- **Must** read `tick_alpha` through `PresentationClock` in presentation only, never in a simulation callable, and **must never** use the tick counter for cosmetic animation phase.
- **Must** keep `Engine.time_scale = 1.0` in release builds; a boot check records `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` in diagnostics otherwise. A boot assertion also requires `application/run/low_processor_mode` to be false (in low-processor mode the engine idles between events, the simulation would stall and the next `delta` would spike), and the diagnostics header records `Engine.max_fps`, the vsync mode and `physics_ticks_per_second`.
- **Must** keep the `delta_us` conversion in `KernelHost` and nowhere else; the lint for forbidden clock APIs (`Time.get_ticks_msec`, `Time.get_ticks_usec`, `get_process_delta_time`, `OS.get_unix_time*`) allow-lists only `KernelHost` and the diagnostics timer. (`OS.get_ticks_*` no longer exists in Godot 4; see `deprecated-apis.md`.)
- **Should** test the driver with injected `delta_us` sequences (16,000 / 16,667 / 17,334 µs patterns, 100 ms hitches, zero-length frames) and the frame order with a recording scene (KRN-LAT-01, KRN-LAT-02).

1	# Godot — Deprecated APIs
2	
3	Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.7 rows); 2026-02-12 (rest)
4	
5	The 4.7 migration guide lists no formal deprecations; the 4.7 rows below are
6	renames and removals from it
7	(https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html).
8	
9	If an agent suggests any API in the "Deprecated" column, it MUST be replaced
10	with the "Use Instead" column.
11	
12	## Nodes & Classes
13	
14	| Deprecated | Use Instead | Since | Notes |
15	|------------|-------------|-------|-------|
16	| `TileMap` | `TileMapLayer` | 4.3 | One node per layer instead of multi-layer node |
17	| `VisibilityNotifier2D` | `VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D` | 4.0 | Renamed for clarity |
18	| `VisibilityNotifier3D` | `VisibleOnScreenNotifier3D` | 4.0 | Renamed for clarity |
19	| `YSort` | `Node2D.y_sort_enabled` | 4.0 | Property on Node2D, not a separate node |
20	| `Navigation2D` / `Navigation3D` | `NavigationServer2D` / `NavigationServer3D` | 4.0 | Server-based API |
21	| `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX` | `EditorSceneFormatImporterFBX2GLTF` | 4.3 | Renamed |
22	
23	## Methods & Properties
24	
25	| Deprecated | Use Instead | Since | Notes |
26	|------------|-------------|-------|-------|
27	| `yield()` | `await signal` | 4.0 | GDScript 2.0 coroutine syntax |
28	| `connect("signal", obj, "method")` | `signal.connect(callable)` | 4.0 | Callable-based connections |
29	| `instance()` | `instantiate()` | 4.0 | Renamed |
30	| `PackedScene.instance()` | `PackedScene.instantiate()` | 4.0 | Renamed |
31	| `get_world()` | `get_world_3d()` | 4.0 | Explicit 2D/3D split |
32	| `OS.get_ticks_msec()` | `Time.get_ticks_msec()` | 4.0 | Time singleton preferred |
33	| `duplicate()` for nested resources | `duplicate_deep()` | 4.5 | Explicit deep copy control |
34	| `Skeleton3D` signal `bone_pose_updated` | `skeleton_updated` | 4.3 | Renamed |
35	| `AnimationPlayer.method_call_mode` | `AnimationMixer.callback_mode_method` | 4.3 | Moved to base class |
36	| `AnimationPlayer.playback_active` | `AnimationMixer.active` | 4.3 | Moved to base class |
37	| `RichTextLabel.ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_IN_PERCENT` | `ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT` | 4.7 | Renamed; GDScript using the old name breaks |
38	| `add_image()` / `update_image()` `width_in_percent`, `height_in_percent` (`bool`) | `width_unit`, `height_unit` (`RichTextLabel.ImageUnit`) | 4.7 | Renamed and retyped |
39	| `DisplayServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` for `Control.accessibility_live` | `AccessibilityServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` | 4.7 | Enum moved to `AccessibilityServer` |
40	| `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.tap_back_pos` | — | 4.7 | Removed |
41	| `EditorSceneFormatImporter.IMPORT_*` constants | `EditorSceneFormatImporter.ImportFlags` enum | 4.7 | Same names, now in an enum |
42	
43	## Patterns (Not Just APIs)
44	
45	| Deprecated Pattern | Use Instead | Why |
46	|--------------------|-------------|-----|
47	| String-based `connect()` | Typed signal connections | Type-safe, refactor-friendly |
48	| `$NodePath` in `_process()` | `@onready var` cached reference | Performance: path lookup every frame |
49	| Untyped `Array` / `Dictionary` | `Array[Type]`, typed variables | GDScript compiler optimizations |
50	| `Texture2D` in `Shader.set_default_texture_parameter()` / `get_default_texture_parameter()` | `Texture` base type | Changed in 4.4; the shading language's `sampler2D` / `texture()` did not change |
51	| Manual post-process viewport chains | `Compositor` + `CompositorEffect` | Structured post-processing (4.3+) |
52	| GodotPhysics3D for new projects | Jolt Physics 3D | Default since 4.6; better stability |
53	| `event.device == 0` to detect mouse or keyboard | `event is InputEventMouse` / `InputEventKey`, or `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD` | Since 4.7 mouse and keyboard no longer report device `0`, which some joypads use |
54	| Installing addons from the editor's AssetLib tab | The editor's Asset Store workspace (4.7+) | 4.7 replaced the Asset Library with the Asset Store |
